name: Guse Connector
author: gusetoaia

sections.description:
Guse Connector links your WooCommerce store to Guse, an order operations platform for Romanian online stores. Orders reach Guse in seconds; from there you generate courier AWBs (FAN Courier, Sameday, Cargus, GLS, DPD), issue invoices (SmartBill, Oblio, FGO, Saga export), handle returns and sync stock across stores. The plugin brings the results back into WooCommerce.

What the plugin does

  • One-click connection. Click “Connect with Guse”, sign in and confirm. The WooCommerce REST API keys are created for you; nothing to copy.
  • Real-time orders and products. Signed webhooks on every new or updated order and product (including variations, stock and barcodes), sent in the background and retried when Guse doesn’t answer. Guse also reconciles every hour.
  • AWBs and invoices in WooCommerce. An “AWB (Guse)” column in the order list and a box on each order with the AWBs (with the courier’s tracking link) and the invoices.
  • Live courier rates at checkout. The “Guse – Courier” shipping method shows one rate per courier connected in Guse, with your markup, rounding and free-shipping rules, plus a fallback rate when Guse can’t be reached. Classic and block checkout.
  • Locker pickup. easybox / Sameday Point and FANbox / PayPoint, chosen on the courier’s official map at checkout.
  • Online returns. A “Return products” page with a two-step return request, an email confirmation with the date and time, a returns register in WooCommerce → Returns and the request sent to Guse. Built to help with the online withdrawal button required in Romania since 2026 (OUG 18/2026); review the texts with your legal advisor.
  • Status and troubleshooting. WooCommerce → Guse Connector shows the connection, the last send, anything not delivered (with “Resend all”) and the WP-Cron queue. Tools → Site Health checks the connection, WP-Cron, HTTPS and the plugin version; logs go to WooCommerce → Status → Logs.
  • Safe on staging. On a copy of the site (staging, clone) the plugin pauses itself, so test orders never overwrite real ones in Guse.
  • HPOS (custom order tables) and cart/checkout blocks compatible. Romanian translation included.

Requirements

A Guse account. You can create one from the plugin page; Guse has a free trial, then a monthly plan. Some features depend on the plan (for example, live rates at checkout need Starter or Pro). Everything the plugin does inside WordPress — the returns form, register and emails — works without a paid plan.

External services

This plugin connects your store to services outside your site. Nothing is sent until you connect the store to Guse, except the courier maps, which load only when a shopper opens them at checkout.

Guse (guse.ro) — the service this plugin connects to, run by the plugin’s author. The plugin sends data to the Guse API at app.guse.ro; the Guse app, where you sign in, is at guse.app.

  • When you connect: the site address and name, and the WooCommerce REST API keys the plugin creates, are sent to Guse. “Connect with Guse” opens guse.app in your browser to sign in and confirm.
  • When an order is created or updated: the order, including the customer’s name, billing and shipping address, email, phone, products, totals, payment and shipping method.
  • When a product is created, updated or deleted: the product (name, SKU, price, stock, barcode, weight, categories, description, variations).
  • At checkout, when the “Guse – Courier” method is enabled: the cart’s products (SKU, quantity, weight, price, shipping class), the destination county, city and postcode and whether the order is cash on delivery, to calculate the rates; and the selected county, to list its cities.
  • In the order screens: the order IDs, to show their AWBs and invoices.
  • When a shopper submits a return request: the request (name, email, products, optional reason and notes, return method and, for cash on delivery, the refund IBAN).
  • Every request carries the plugin version; deactivating the plugin tells Guse it was deactivated.

Terms: https://guse.ro/termeni — Privacy policy: https://guse.ro/confidentialitate

Sameday locker map (cdn.sameday.ro) — when a shopper clicks “Choose easybox” at checkout, the Sameday map script is loaded from Sameday’s servers and shows its easybox and Sameday Point locations. The shopper’s browser connects directly to Sameday. Terms: https://sameday.ro/termeni-si-conditii/

FAN Courier map (api.fancourier.ro, tile.openstreetmap.org) — when a shopper clicks “Choose FANbox” at checkout, the FAN Courier map included in the plugin reads the pickup points from FAN Courier’s API and the map tiles from OpenStreetMap, directly from the shopper’s browser. FAN Courier: https://www.fancourier.ro/conditii-generale-privind-furnizarea-serviciilor-postale — privacy: https://www.fancourier.ro/politica-de-confidentialitate/ — OpenStreetMap tile policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ — privacy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Third-party libraries

  • assets/vendor/map-fanbox-points/ — map-fanbox-points 0.1.1 by FAN Courier, MIT license, the unmodified UMD build from https://www.npmjs.com/package/map-fanbox-points (it bundles React, MUI and Leaflet).
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress go to Plugins → Add New Plugin, search for “Guse Connector”, install and activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. WooCommerce → Guse Connector opens. Click “Connect with Guse”, sign in to Guse (or create an account) and confirm the store.
  3. For courier rates at checkout: WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → your zone (e.g. Romania) → add the “Guse – Courier” method.
  4. Check the online returns page and texts in WooCommerce → Returns → Settings.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Guse account?

Yes. The plugin connects WooCommerce to Guse, where AWBs, invoices and returns are handled. You can create an account from WooCommerce → Guse Connector → “Create a free account”.

My store was already connected in Guse with REST API keys.

Click “Connect with Guse”: the same site keeps its store, orders and settings in Guse; the plugin just replaces the keys.

Why does Guse ask for HTTPS?

WooCommerce accepts REST API keys only over HTTPS. Without it, webhooks and checkout rates still work, but Guse can’t import past orders or update stock and prices in the store.

What happens on a staging copy of my site?

The plugin notices that it runs on a different address than the one it was connected on and stops sending anything to Guse, so test orders don’t overwrite real ones. Reconnect it if the store moved to the new address.

Orders don’t reach Guse.

Open WooCommerce → Guse Connector: it shows the connection, the last error and the queue. If WP-Cron doesn’t run (for example DISABLE_WP_CRON without a system cron job), orders wait in the queue; Tools → Site Health says so too.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

The store is disconnected in Guse, the plugin’s REST API keys are revoked and its settings removed. The returns register stays in the database, because it is the record of your customers’ withdrawal requests.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • The button that sends the online return request now reads “Confirm withdrawal” (in Romanian, “Confirmați retragerea”), the exact wording required by art. 11¹ para. (6) of OUG 34/2014.

1.0.4

  • Guse Connector is now in the WordPress.org plugin directory: from this version on, updates come from WordPress.org, like any other plugin.

1.0.3

  • Fewer admin notices: they appear only on the Plugins screen and WooCommerce pages, and activating the plugin no longer redirects to its page.
  • The city dropdown at checkout and the “Refresh” button in the order box are protected by a security token.

1.0.2

  • Courier rates at checkout refresh every 10 minutes: a cart that is already open picks up the changes made in Guse → Shipping rates (a new courier, a pickup point option, another markup).

1.0.1

  • Clearer labels: the address the plugin connects to is shown as the Guse API URL.

1.0.0

  • “Connect with Guse”: connect the store in one click from WordPress (sign in to Guse and confirm), or create a Guse account right from the plugin.
  • “Update now” notice when Guse needs a newer plugin version; the Guse card of the store shows the plugin version.
  • Status on WooCommerce → Guse Connector: last successful send, last error, sends not delivered with “Resend all”, the WP-Cron queue and the automatic updates setting.
  • Tools → Site Health: checks for the Guse connection, WP-Cron, HTTPS and the plugin version, plus a Guse Connector section for support.
  • Logs in WooCommerce → Status → Logs (source “guse-connector”).
  • Getting started steps after activation; deactivating the plugin tells Guse and clears its queue, reactivating resumes pending return requests.
  • Privacy: suggested privacy policy text, export and erasure of return requests’ personal data.
  • Clean uninstall: the store is disconnected in Guse, API keys revoked, settings removed (the returns register stays).
  • The FAN Courier map is included in the plugin instead of being loaded from a CDN.
  • English source texts with the Romanian translation included.

0.10.5

  • Return emails use the store’s WooCommerce email design.

0.10.0

  • Online returns (OUG 18/2026): “Return products” page, two-step request, email confirmation, returns register, sent to Guse.

0.9.0

  • Automatic updates, webhook retries, key revocation on reconnect/disconnect, real connection status, staging copies paused.

0.5.0

  • FANbox and PayPoint pickup on the official FAN Courier map.

0.3.0

  • easybox / Sameday Point pickup at checkout.

0.2.0

  • “Guse – Courier” shipping method with live courier rates and a city dropdown.

0.1.0

  • First version: pairing, signed webhooks, AWB column and order box.
